prompt: After `bin/version` was built, `version.txt` was changed to `1.5.0` and the same binary run again. What did it print, and why?

choices.text: `1.5.0`, because the file is read at start-up
choices.why: Nothing reads the disk; the variable was filled at build time.

choices.text: `1.4.2`, copied in at build time
choices.why: Right. Only a new build picked up `1.5.0`.

choices.text: An error, because the embedded file changed
choices.why: The binary does not know the file changed.

choices.text: An empty version
choices.why: The contents are inside the binary and do not disappear.

prompt: A colleague deletes `logo.txt` by mistake and rebuilds. What happens?
hint: The first build in the lesson had no banner yet.

choices.text: It builds, and `logo` is empty
choices.why: A pattern that matches nothing is refused, so no binary ships without its file.

choices.text: It builds, and the old banner is reused from the cache
choices.why: The build reads the source tree; a missing file is an error.

choices.text: The build fails on the missing pattern
choices.why: Right, which is what makes an embedded file safe to rely on.

choices.text: It panics when it starts
choices.why: It never gets that far: there is no binary.

prompt: Why must a file with `//go:embed` import `embed`, even as `import _ "embed"`?
hint: What would a forgotten directive look like without the check?

choices.text: A forgotten one fails instead of going empty
choices.why: Right. A directive is a comment, and the import is what the go command checks.

choices.text: Because `embed` contains the files at run time
choices.why: The files are in the variable; the package is the marker.

choices.text: The import makes the binary smaller
choices.why: It has nothing to do with size.

choices.text: Only for a `[]byte` variable
choices.why: `version` was a `string` and the rule held there too.

prompt: The directive is written as a comment, with no space after the slashes: `//go:___ version.txt`.
`//go:embed static` brought in `index.html` and `style.css` but not `.draft.html` or `_notes.txt`. What brings in all four?

choices.text: `//go:embed static/*.*`
choices.why: The lesson used a prefix, not a glob; `all:` is what it showed taking everything.

choices.text: `//go:embed all:static`
choices.why: Right: the second variable got all four.

choices.text: Renaming them without the prefix characters
choices.why: That changes the files, not the pattern; `all:` keeps their names.

choices.text: An `embed.FS` cannot hold them
choices.why: `everything` held them.

prompt: Why does `//go:embed` leave out files starting with `.` or `_` by default?
hint: Think of a `.env` in the directory.

choices.text: Hidden files cannot be read by the go command
choices.why: `all:` reads them fine.

choices.text: So a `.env` cannot ship by accident
choices.why: Right. Leaving them out is the safe default; `all:` is a decision.

choices.text: To keep the binary under a size limit
choices.why: There is no such limit in the lesson.

choices.text: Because Windows forbids such names
choices.why: The rule is about what is likely to be private, not about any system.

prompt: `static.ReadFile("index.html")` failed with `file does not exist`, though the page was embedded. Why?
hint: Look at the paths the listing printed.

choices.text: Embedded files are read only once
choices.why: The previous line read it fine as `static/index.html`.

choices.text: HTML files need `all:`
choices.why: `all:` is about names starting with `.` or `_`.

choices.text: Its path keeps the directory: `static/index.html`
choices.why: Right. `fs.Sub` is how the next section drops the prefix.

choices.text: `ReadFile` only works on a disk
choices.why: It is a method of `embed.FS` and worked on the full path.

prompt: A function takes an `fs.FS` and reads `config.json` from it. In tests it is given `os.DirFS("testdata")`; in production, an `embed.FS` narrowed with `fs.Sub`. What makes that work?
hint: What do both values have in common, errors included?

choices.text: `embed.FS` converts itself to a directory on disk
choices.why: Nothing is written to disk; it is read-only and in memory.

choices.text: Both are an `fs.FS`, with the same errors
choices.why: Right: `fs.ErrNotExist` in both, so the function need not know which.

choices.text: `fs.Sub` copies the embedded files into `testdata`
choices.why: `fs.Sub` only narrows a view to a sub-directory.

choices.text: The go command swaps them during `go test`
choices.why: The test passes a different value; nothing is swapped behind it.

prompt: Why did a request for `/` find `index.html`, when the embedded path is `static/index.html`?
hint: What did the program do with `files` before serving it?

choices.text: `FileServerFS` strips any first directory
choices.why: It serves the paths it is given; the stripping happened before.

choices.text: The browser adds `/static`
choices.why: curl asked for `/` and nothing added anything.

choices.text: `all:` was used
choices.why: `serve/main.go` embeds plain `static`; `_notes.txt` was a 404.

choices.text: `fs.Sub(files, "static")` made `static` the root
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Fine, if the file starts with `_`

choices.text: No: it differs, so it is read at run time
choices.why: Right. Embedded files are fixed at build time, the same in every copy.

choices.text: No: an `embed.FS` cannot hold JSON
